title: The Radiators of the coast road
premise: Sebastian Quintana, a piano tuner who reads the past in the hum of old radiators, has spent thirty years in his late aunt's coastal house as a caretaker who never claimed it. When a box of undelivered letters surfaces behind the wardrobe, he learns she hid evidence that her husband's death was no accident—and that Sebastian's own father, the town's beloved constable, covered it up. As the letters pull him toward the surviving daughter of the dead man, Sebastian must choose between protecting his father's memory and delivering a justice the law will never pursue. In the end, he mails the letters, confesses publicly at the memorial concert he finally tunes the hall piano for, and loses the house but gains, for the first time, an actual life.
about_author: Ansel Zhou is a former piano restorer who spent a decade working the coastal towns of the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction. Their stories dwell on quiet houses, inherited guilt, and the small mechanical objects that outlive the people who owned them.

chapters.title: The Hum Beneath the Floor
chapters.summary: Sebastian, tuning a piano in a decaying seaside hotel, explains through his own POV how radiators carry the history of houses—heat, rust, the knock of pipes. He returns to his aunt Marisol's house, where he lives like a tenant, keeping lists of repairs he never makes. Emotional beat: comfortable numbness on the edge of change.

chapters.title: What the Wardrobe Kept
chapters.summary: Moving the wardrobe to fix a warped floorboard, Sebastian finds a tin box: forty-one letters, stamped, sealed, never mailed, all addressed to Elena Vasquez. The earliest is dated two weeks after the drowning of Elena's father, Tomás, in 1989. POV: Sebastian. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread as he recognizes his father's name in the margins.

chapters.title: Letters Written in Winter
chapters.summary: Sebastian reads the letters in order—Marisol's voice emerging: grief, then suspicion about the night Tomás drowned, then fear of someone she calls only 'the uniform.' Intercut with Sebastian's memories of his father, Constable Quintana, the town's sainted figure. POV: Sebastian with letter excerpts. Beat: the ground tilting under a childhood idol.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Answers Doors Slowly
chapters.summary: Sebastian tracks Elena to a garden nursery two towns over. She is wary, sharp-tongued, still angry at Marisol for decades of silence. She doesn't know the letters exist; she thought Marisol simply stopped writing. POV shifts to Elena. Beat: two lonely people circling a shared wound, neither ready to open it.

chapters.title: A Tuner's Ear for Lies
chapters.summary: Sebastian begins investigating the drowning using what he knows of the house itself—the radiator in the back room that was replaced the winter after Tomás died, the receipt hidden with the letters. His father's old case notes surface at the county archive. POV: Sebastian. Beat: obsession replacing drift; the price of survival starts coming due.

chapters.title: Elena's Version of the Water
chapters.summary: Elena recounts her father's last night: a dispute with a developer over the coastal lots, a phone call from the constable, a body found where currents don't go. She reveals she once confronted Marisol and was turned away. POV: Elena. Beat: grief given shape; the first fragile alliance between them.

chapters.title: The Uniform in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Sebastian finds the photograph Marisol kept: his father and the developer, shaking hands on the dock, dated the day before the drowning. The developer's son now sits on the town council and is pushing to demolish the house. POV: Sebastian. Beat: love against duty—he must betray either his father or the truth.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Sebastian confronts the councilman's family quietly; the son offers him money for the letters and the house, revealing the family always knew. Sebastian refuses but realizes going public means destroying his father's name and Elena's last hope of legal remedy—the statute long expired. POV: Sebastian. Beat: rising tension; justice outside the law becomes the only road.

chapters.title: Forty-One Letters
chapters.summary: Climax. At the town's centennial concert, Sebastian tunes the hall piano, then instead of playing intermission music, reads Marisol's final letter aloud from the stage, naming his father and the developer. The room fractures; the councilman's son storms out; Elena stands and takes Sebastian's hand. POV alternates between them. Beat: catharsis, exposure, no way back.

chapters.title: The House Lets Go
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, the house is sold to settle the storm of attention; Sebastian mails the remaining letters to their addresses anyway, one by one. He and Elena tune the old radiator together—a small ritual of beginning. He signs his first lease under his own name. POV: Sebastian closing into shared narration. Beat: forgiveness of the stranger in the photographs, and of himself.
